entities.summary:
Plotinus was a Hellenistic Greek philosopher, born and raised in Roman Egypt, who is regarded by modern scholarship as the founder of Neoplatonism.




He studied under the tutelage of Ammonius Saccas and later tutored several notable philosophers, including Porphyry and Iamblichus.




Plotinus' philosophical system synthesized elements of Plato's philosophy with Middle Platonism and mysticism, emphasizing the attainment of spiritual enlightenment through the contemplation of the One and the rejection of the material world.

















Plotinus' works include the Enneads, a collection of 7 volumes of philosophical treatises, which provide insight into his metaphysical, epistemological, and ethical views.






Plotinus' ideas had a profound impact on Western philosophy, influencing Christian theology, Renaissance humanism, and modern philosophical movements.




Plotinus died at the age of 70 in Rome, leaving behind a legacy of philosophical thought that continues to be studied and debated by scholars today.
